objective: Extend the raw DR24 Workbench browser smoke to seven OIDs selected from five BTS-associated spatial candidate identifiers, and validate the sample manifest without approving physical-source grouping.
previous_knowledge_consumed: The five-OID smoke passed for 650 epochs in run 42232639126.
Four OIDs have independent HATS payload hashes; three additional candidate OIDs have availability-only evidence.
The DR24 BTS availability artifact includes OID 347104300029855 with 368 epochs and OID 725113200004086 with 1165 epochs.
These are spatial candidate associations, not confirmed physical identities.
The 50-row table cap is a maximum; shorter light curves display all available rows.

baseline.revision: PR #267 Workbench branch plus PR #272 five-OID smoke
baseline.description: Raw-only DR24 Explorer. No model, feature, taxonomy, benchmark, or release changes.

correctness.before: Five-OID browser smoke covered three BTS-associated candidate identifiers and 650 epochs.
correctness.after: The seven-OID test covers five BTS-associated candidate identifiers and 2183 expected epochs. Four OIDs have independent payload hashes; three are checked for availability, epoch parity, chart count and SHA-256 format. Live rerun is pending.

reproducibility.before: Five-OID sample was not linked to a machine-readable candidate sample manifest.
reproducibility.after: A versioned sample manifest records the BTS/DR24 source artifacts, hashes, candidate IDs, OIDs, filters, epoch counts, angular separations and explicit no-grouping policy. The test checks manifest/OID/hash consistency.

reliability.after: The test now covers 7 OIDs and verifies the 50-row cap, including the 24-row short curve and longer 368- and 1165-epoch curves. Live rerun is pending.

scientific_validity.reason: Candidate spatial associations do not confirm physical identity. No OID grouping, photometry normalization, QC selection, feature generation, inference, calibration, OOD or anomaly evaluation is performed.

measurement.trade_off: Use seven OIDs across five BTS-associated candidate IDs. This is a raw lookup sample, not a confirmed five-object scientific sample. Three OIDs lack independent payload-hash references.

evidence: BTS-to-DR24 spatial recovery artifact 13179927852, ZIP SHA-256 dbbd39759d11645cfa044538d786960b3bf221d25a9b73b849f136a735e1f830.
DR24 lightcurve availability artifact 13184608092, ZIP SHA-256 84548734b39fa5e1639e6b06ed54d0630c23603b4c6a803b3e7c0935966de7e3.
Manifest totals: five candidate external IDs, seven OIDs, 2183 catalog epochs; four OIDs have independent HATS payload hashes and three do not.
The test verifies that the manifest OID set and hash-reference map exactly match the pinned browser test expectations.
The seven-OID live browser workflow must pass before this cycle is marked verified.

unresolved: Run the seven-OID live browser workflow and inspect its evidence artifact.
Acquire independent payload-hash references for the three OIDs without them.
The five BTS identifiers remain spatial candidates; physical-source identity is not confirmed.
A 5–10 object application acceptance test still requires validated source mapping, descriptive QC, exports and a reproducibility bundle.

findings: The candidate manifest must keep OID identifiers separate from BTS external identifiers.
A spatial candidate match is not an approved cross-OID grouping rule.
A raw smoke can validate retrieval and display without claiming scientific identity.

open_blockers: Independently verify the three additional payload hashes.
Do not use candidate associations as training labels or model evaluation ground truth.
Add descriptive raw QC diagnostics, exports and a complete reproducibility bundle.
Complete the 30–50 object guided Park demonstration.

knowledge_carried_forward: Keep the candidate sample raw-only and explicitly marked as spatial candidate associations.
Do not count OIDs as astrophysical objects.
Do not group OIDs without independent identity evidence.
Do not filter catflags or relabel HMJD.
Keep DR24 raw exploration separate from frozen v0.2.0 inference.
